questions_and_answers.question: A Phillips curve implies a. a negative relationship between consumption and saving. b. a positive relationship between inflation and prices. c. a negative relationship between inflation and unemployment. d. a positive relationship between consumption expenditure and inflation.
questions_and_answers.answer: The answer is C. This is a definitional question about what the Phillips Curve shows. When unemployment is increasing, consumers won't spend as much and inflation (prices) decreases. When unemployment is falling, consumers will spending more causing an increase in prices (inflation). Here is a typical example of a short run Phillips curve: As you can see, when inflation is high, unemployment is low. When unemployment is low, inflation is high. The other answers are all relationships that macroeconomists care about, however they aren't what is graphed on a Phillips curve.

questions_and_answers.question: A Phillips curve implies a negative relationship between: A. inflation and unemployment B. aggregate price level and real GDP C. inflation and prices D. consumption and saving E. consumption and inflation
questions_and_answers.answer: A Phillips curve implies a negative relationship between inflation and unemployment (option A). This concept was introduced by economist A.W. Phillips, who found that when inflation is high, unemployment tends to be low, and vice versa. This inverse relationship occurs because higher inflation often results from increased demand for goods and services, leading to more production, which in turn requires more labor, thus lowering unemployment. Conversely, when inflation is low, demand is typically weaker, leading to reduced production and higher unemployment rates. So, the correct answer is A: inflation and unemployment. learn more about Phillips curve here:brainly.com/question/14339149 #SPJ11
